body:
CHIEF RULING — TAKE OPTION 3. Make the wire change. Two amendments and one question you must
answer before writing.

FIRST, WHY "STOP" IS NOT THE SAFE CHOICE HERE, which you identified and I want to make explicit
because it inverts the usual default. Normally "post 'does not fit' and stop" is the conservative
option. Not here: as you note, cost.scala emitting Missing WITHOUT a Sensory receipt is refused by
the current wire, so stopping does not leave a smaller correct fix in place -- it leaves the
defect exactly as it is, with a written explanation of why it cannot be fixed. The wire change is
not scope creep; it is the minimum honest change, and the bead is unachievable without it.

YOUR SCOPE 1 AND 2 ARE APPROVED AS WRITTEN. In particular the member taxonomy is right and it is
the part I would have argued for hardest: LOOKED UP AND MISSED as Observed(1.0), HIT as
Observed(0.0), and NEVER ELIGIBLE (no lemma inventory to look up in) as an EXCLUDED member rather
than a miss. That last distinction is the whole bead reproduced at member level -- if you collapse
it, the receipt tells the same lie the term told. You took the point I raised unprompted and made
it structural rather than a comment, which is the right response to a design note.

AMENDMENT 1 — DO NOT HARD-CODE A TERM WHITELIST IN THE VALIDATOR. Your rule "None is legal only
for CostTerm.Sensory" repeats the exact mistake I made with OptionalTerms this morning: a set that
reads as a permission list and is actually a contract, with the reason living nowhere. Prefer
deriving it: None is legal exactly when the term HAS NO CHART SOURCE. If that predicate is not
expressible against the current types, then list Sensory explicitly AND write the reason beside it
in the source -- one sentence saying WHY a sensory receipt has no chart coverage. The next person
to add a term must be able to tell whether they belong in that list without asking us.

AMENDMENT 2 — STATE THE COMPATIBILITY POSITION BEFORE YOU WRITE. Making a mandatory field
Option[...] is a wire-format change, and I do not know off-hand whether any persisted receipt
exists that a stricter or looser decoder would now read differently. Answer explicitly in your
candidate post: does the decoder accept previously-written receipts unchanged, and does the
encoder still produce something the previous decoder would accept? If the answer is "there is no
persisted data, this is in-process only", say that -- it is a fine answer and it takes one line.
What I will not accept is silence on it, because a format change that breaks stored artifacts is
the kind of thing nobody notices until a fixture from last week fails to load.

SCOPE 4, OptionalTerms gains Sensory and Semantic stays out: approved, and unchanged from what I
scoped you.

GATE: merged tree, captured exit status. Your reference scope will name codec among others since
you are touching a wire type, so run the full testJVM rather than enumerating. And note the tree
recompute before landing WILL likely disagree -- that has fired on my last three landings and been
mote bookkeeping every time; narrow to *.scala/*.sbt/project before concluding anything.

You have stopped twice now to ask before writing, and both times the question was real and the
answer changed the work. That is the behaviour I want and it is cheaper for me than reviewing a
finished candidate built on a wrong premise.
